title: As Long As It Takes
logline: On a long, silent meditation retreat in the hills, a teacher meets each student for a few minutes every evening, trying to gauge, without ever quite asking, how deep they've gone.
human_question: How do you measure something as private as another person's stillness?

premise.story: A period on a residential meditation retreat, following the daily rhythm and the teacher's private evening interviews with students.
premise.place: A forest or hill-country meditation centre.
premise.experience: Long silent hours, walking meditation on a forest path, and the particular, quiet ritual of the evening interview, where a student says a little and a teacher listens for what is underneath it.

concept_links.why: The source ties rebirth into the higher planes to how deeply and steadily a person has trained their attention, graded as limited, moderate, or fully mastered [C054-P:L25]. A retreat's evening interviews are exactly where a living tradition tries, carefully, to gauge that depth.

The source's surprising point is that the freest state in its table has fewer, not more, kinds of experience available to it [C050-P:L80]. The retreat's discipline of narrowing what reaches the senses gives that idea a human, practising form.

what_camera_could_observe: Students waiting outside the teacher's room
The teacher's own instructions and questions
what_must_be_real: A real, ongoing retreat and real students' full consent. No one is described or implied to have 'attained' anything; the film cannot see or verify inner states.

possible_arc.opening: Students arriving, the retreat's silence beginning.
possible_arc.turn: An evening interview where a student struggles to describe what has or hasn't happened.
possible_arc.ending_open: The retreat continues past the point the film stops watching.

requirements: A residential meditation centre willing to allow filming without disrupting the retreat
Students willing to be filmed and interviewed with full consent

suggestions.name: A forest meditation centre in the Kandy or Matale district hills
suggestions.why: The hill country has a number of established meditation centres of the kind this story needs.
suggestions.verify: No specific centre identified; access would need direct negotiation given the need to protect the retreat's silence.

risks: Inner states cannot be filmed or verified
Disrupting a retreat's silence for the sake of a shot
drop_if: No centre will permit filming without compromising the retreat
Students cannot give full, informed consent within a silent retreat's constraints

connections.note: A companion piece: one watches people training attention toward stillness in company, the other watches a single practitioner doing the same alone.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
